title: Getting the Love You Want: A Guide for Couples
author: Harville Hendrix, Ph.D.
target_audience: Couples seeking to strengthen or repair their relationship
Individuals wanting to understand romantic dynamics
Therapists and counselors working with couples
Anyone interested in personal growth in the context of love and partnership
core_themes: Childhood influences on adult romantic behavior
Healing and growing together as partners
primary_purpose: To help couples understand and resolve recurring conflicts by uncovering the hidden roots of relationship struggles and providing practical exercises for deeper emotional connection, healing, and lasting intimacy.

structure_format.narrative_style: Supportive, instructive, blend of anecdote and psychology
structure_format.organization: Organized into three main parts: understanding relationship patterns, learning new strategies for connection, and applying practical techniques

key_concepts_lessons: Imago theory: Our attraction patterns are shaped by unmet needs and wounds from childhood.
Unconscious motivations influence whom and how we love.
Transformation requires both partners' commitment to growth and conscious communication.
Listening empathetically and practicing 'intentional dialogue' can break destructive cycles.
Replacing blame and criticism with curiosity and understanding fosters mutual healing.
Growth, not just compatibility, is at the heart of successful long-term relationships.
notable_features: Introduction of Imago Relationship Therapy principles
Guided exercises for couples to complete together
Widely used in workshops and counseling practices
References both academic research and personal experience
cultural_historical_context: Published in the late 1980s when popular psychology and self-help movements were growing, the book tapped into a new demand for practical, emotionally focused relationship advice. Its influence continued through multiple revisions, addressing evolving conversations about intimacy, therapy, and personal growth.
reception_impact: Became a landmark title in couples therapy; over 4 million copies sold
Praised by therapists and marriage counselors as a foundational text
Helped popularize the Imago therapy model used worldwide
Critics note its approach may simplify complex psychological issues; some debate about universal applicability
